notes:
Summary: mid-market product analytics SaaS (B2B) evaluating Redwood as replacement for ProviderX. Primary driver: reduce per-token cost and get predictable latency under heavy dashboard traffic. Secondary: stronger ops + observability for SLOs. Current setup: ProviderX API + in-house caching layer, ~10k requests/day, spikes to 1.2x on billing cycles.

POC status: running on Redwood Hosted via a compatibility shim that maps ProviderX endpoints to Redwood API. We shipped a small adapter to keep prompt/format parity and to re-use existing instrumentation. Initial runs show token count delta ~+4% (tokenization differences) and one prompt ('policy_summary') shows >5% change vs baseline in semantic similarity score — engineering investigating prompt tweaks and temperature/stop-token configs.

Technical asks from customer: VPC connectivity for Dedicated, KMS integration, audit logs retained 1 year, SSO via SAML, ability to pin model versions and fallback policies (ProviderX -> Redwood aliasing). They want a predictable canary strategy (5% traffic) for first week of live migration.

Commercial: finance is evaluating TCO vs ProviderX. Customer asked for a line-item comparison (token pricing + Dedicated reserved pool cost + support). Pricing deck shared: drive://canyonbridge/poc-pricing-v1. Sales note: aim for 3–6 month pilot, convert to 12-month Dedicated if ROI met.

Risks & mitigations:
- Prompt parity/regressions: building automated evals + daily drift alerts; keep ProviderX as fallback for first 2 weeks of live migration.
- Tokenization/cost variance: include quantile token burn report and tune batching/KV cache.
- Contractual billing: need to map ProviderX committed discounts to Redwood pricing model; finance call scheduled.
